clue.text: Union leader located in many a plant

indicators.note: located in says one piece is set within the letters of the other

parts.note: lots means many

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from Union

explanation.surface: A trade union boss is found inside a great many factories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory in the union story, but it is the definition: a water plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, a flowering aquatic species.

clue.text: Weariness of student when taking on new duties

indicators.note: taking on means adding a further piece after the first ones

parts.note: L, from learner plates, stands for a student
as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: new says the following word is made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A pupil grows tired on being given fresh tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges DUTIES into SITUDE, which L and AS take on.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is physical or mental tiredness, a lack of energy.

clue.text: Ruffian gives up books? Disgusting!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the letters run upwards, so backwards

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A thug abandons reading, finding it revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives up' looks like quitting, but 'up' reverses OT to TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough is a violent street thug or hooligan.

clue.text: Unhesitatingly make defamatory remarks about the troubled islands

indicators.note: about puts the shortened word round the jumbled one
unhesitatingly means without the hesitation sound er

parts.note: to slander is to make false and damaging statements

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the following word's letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Without pause, someone slanders the strife-torn islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unhesitatingly' drops ER (a hesitation) from SLANDER, leaving SLAND; 'troubled' turns THE into HET, which SLAND goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shetland is a group of Scottish islands north of the mainland.

clue.text: Ruthless, reversing vehicle into a' couple of fellows

indicators.note: into says the turned vehicle goes inside the first fellow's name

parts.note: a don is a university fellow; the first of the two men

indicators.note: reversing tells us the word for the vehicle is read backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
Ian is a man's name, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: A heartless driver backs a car into two men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vehicle' turned by 'reversing' sits 'into' the first fellow. The mark after 'a' on the page is a printing smudge, and 'a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Draconian laws are harsh and severe, named after the strict Athenian lawgiver Draco.

clue.text: Democrat who designed a lateen-rigged vessel

indicators.note: designed means made up, so the letters of the next word are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A Democratic politician who drew up plans for a sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges WHO into HOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhow is an Arab boat with triangular sails, the kind called lateen.

clue.text: First-class copper recently defending right to speak

indicators.note: defending means guarding, so the first word surrounds the abbreviation for right

parts.note: A1 means first-class; the 1 is read as the letter I
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
late means recently, as in 'of late'

explanation.surface: A top policeman lately standing up for free speech.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is the old shipping-register mark for first-class, its 1 read as I. 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To articulate is to express words clearly, to utter them.

clue.text: Unrepeatable event for somebody with the cricket side

parts.note: one means somebody, as in 'one does one's best'
the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A unique occasion for a player in the cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the leg side; 'side' looks like a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off is something that happens just once and will not recur.

clue.text: Very soon Jack turned up with a sweetheart

parts.note: in a mo, short for in a moment, means very soon

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up says the word for Jack is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: jack and tar are both old names for a sailor

explanation.surface: Any minute now Jack arrives with his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like arrived, but it reverses TAR into RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman who is loved, a female lover.

clue.text: Famous saw?

explanation.surface: A well-known proverb?
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like a noun, an old proverb; it is the past tense of see.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known; to have noted something is to have observed it.

clue.text: Use a cab to switch characters in jug

indicators.note: switching the characters means the letters of the phrase before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instruction to swap people around by taking a taxi into a jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to switch characters' rearranges USE A CAB TO; 'to' belongs to the fodder, not just the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauce-boat is a jug-like vessel with a lip for pouring gravy.

clue.text: Insist on being strict

explanation.surface: Someone demands to be severe.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to demand payment or compliance; exact also means precise and rigorous.

clue.text: Get inspiration during salute, say

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: say signals that a word is to be taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: to hail someone is to salute or greet them

explanation.surface: Someone becomes inspired while giving a salute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiration' here is literal: drawing breath in. HAIL and HALE sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiration in its physical sense is breathing in air.

clue.text: Where Casement died, betrayed outside a common eating-place

indicators.note: outside says the first word's letters wrap round the second's

parts.note: sold, as in sold out, means betrayed
a caff is a cheap British cafe, a slang word for an ordinary eating house

explanation.surface: A history note: the Irish rebel was betrayed somewhere near a cheap diner.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger Casement, Irish nationalist, was hanged for treason in 1916. CAFF is British slang for a basic cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: Casement was executed by hanging, and a gallows platform is where condemned prisoners die.

clue.text: Muse, possibly, about Genghis Khan's people discovering bones

indicators.note: about puts the jumbled letters round the name of the people
possibly says the word Muse can be rearranged into another form

parts.note: the Tatars were among the steppe peoples of Genghis Khan's empire

explanation.surface: A poet's muse contemplates the Mongol hordes while finding skeletons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges Muse into a form that splits round the people named, 'about' them; 'discovering' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The metatarsus is the group of five long foot bones between ankle and toes.

clue.text: Rude, almost, rejecting article by international representative

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two parts sit side by side

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, is the standard abbreviation for an international body
our man somewhere is our representative there

indicators.note: rejecting says the article is thrown out of the word meaning almost

parts.note: nearly means almost
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A diplomat from abroad is described as almost rude when turning things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' looks like it qualifies 'Rude', but it is the word for almost, from which 'rejecting' throws out the article; 'by' sets it beside the diplomat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking manners means being impolite and discourteous.

clue.text: Note the wide difference ol feeling about Northern Ireland's system

parts.note: me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: about says the gap word goes round the abbreviation for the province

parts.note: a chasm is a deep divide, figuratively a gulf in opinion
NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A remark on the deep split in opinion over Northern Ireland's political arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a remark; it is a note of the sol-fa scale. 'about' wraps the gulf round the province's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanism is the working arrangement of parts, a process or setup.

clue.text: Young creature offered a member's back

explanation.surface: A young animal is offered by someone in a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A calf is a young cow; it is also the fleshy rear of a leg, which is a limb or member.

clue.text: Competition to win buckshee engraving implement

parts.note: buckshee is British slang for free of charge
a style, or stylus, is a pointed tool for engraving

explanation.surface: A contest where the prize is a free engraving tool.
explanation.walkthrough: BUCKSHEE is old British army slang meaning free.
explanation.definitionFit: Freestyle is a contest class, as in swimming or wrestling, with few restrictions on technique.

clue.text: Infirm and lacking capacity to cross street

indicators.note: to cross means to straddle, so the street abbreviation sits across the word inside

parts.note: unable means lacking the ability or capacity

explanation.surface: An elderly person, frail and unable to get across the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cross' means to straddle: the word for lacking capacity spans the road abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Unstable means weak and unsteady, as a frail person may be.

clue.text: Eat out in an Oxford Street chophouse

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow, across Street and chophouse

explanation.surface: Dine out at a restaurant on a famous London shopping street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat out' suggests a restaurant meal; here it means corrode, as acid does. Oxford Street is London's main shopping street.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to let acid corrode a design into metal.

clue.text: Involved in alarm, get the strap

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting caught up in an alarm, someone is punished with a belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' rearranges IN ALARM GET. 'get the strap' reads as a beating; the strap is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A martingale is a strap on a horse's harness that stops it tossing its head.

clue.text: Some say class will cause persistent resentment

indicators.note: some say signals that a phrase is to be taken as it is spoken

parts.note: rank means class or social standing; will contracts to 'll, as in 'it'll'

explanation.surface: People claim social status breeds lasting bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: RANK'LL, 'class will', is pronounced the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to keep irritating, leaving a lingering grudge.

clue.text: Young hooligan's rip-off

explanation.surface: A young thug's swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearaway is a reckless young troublemaker; to tear away is to rip something off.

clue.text: Slightly upset when one breaks this bone?

indicators.note: breaks says one letter goes into the middle of the other piece
in a down clue, upset says the phrase is turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a bit means slightly
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A mild fracture: is this the bone you broke?
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns A BIT into TIBA, and 'breaks' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, the larger lower-leg bone.

clue.text: Supplies of clerical wear

explanation.surface: Provisions of priestly clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocks are reserves of goods; a stock is also a band worn round a clergyman's neck.

clue.text: Cloudless plain

explanation.surface: A clear sky on the plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear skies have no cloud; something clear is also obvious and easy to understand.

clue.text: An old prime minister's horse

explanation.surface: A former British leader's steed.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles, 2nd Earl Grey, led the government that passed the 1832 Reform Act.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl Grey was British prime minister in the 1830s; a grey is a white-coated horse.

clue.text: Bishop found gamble enlivening

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a risk is a gamble

explanation.surface: A churchman finds a bet exciting.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisk weather or air is bracing and refreshing.

clue.text: Quiet, springy environment for woody plants

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
rubbery things are bouncy and springy

explanation.surface: A calm, bouncy setting for trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrubbery is a garden area planted with bushes, which are woody plants.

clue.text: 50 miles, say, to travel without any direction .

indicators.note: to travel suggests moving about, so these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Driving fifty miles or so just to wander about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to travel' rearranges L (50 in Roman numerals) with MILES and SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something aimlessly means doing it with no purpose or goal.

clue.text: From which flyers keep a state in view

indicators.note: in places the state's abbreviation inside the word for view

parts.note: to eye something is to view it
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: Pilots maintain a nation within sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyers' are birds, not pilots, and 'keep' means dwell. 'a state' is RI, Rhode Island, not a country.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest high on a crag, where birds of prey live.
